title: Three pitfalls: で, が and に
summary: Three small kana each do two different jobs: で (particle or te-form of だ), が (subject marker or "but") and に (target or an old "and"). Look at what comes before and what ends the phrase.

blocks.text: Three look-alikes catch learners out. For each pair there is one job you know and one you may not.

As a **particle**, で follows a noun and marks where an action happens or the means used: 図書館で勉強する. As the **て-form of だ**, it connects descriptions or clauses: さくらはきれいで優しい. It also hides in phrases such as お元気で ("take care") and 無事でよかった ("I'm glad you're safe").

blocks.jp: さくらはきれいで優しい。

blocks.text: As a **subject particle**, が always follows a noun. As a **connector**, が follows a complete clause (ending in a verb, an adjective or だ) and means "but". It can also end a sentence, leaving the rest unsaid and polite.

blocks.jp: お店に行ったが、パンがなかった。
blocks.en: I went to the shop, but there was no bread.

blocks.jp: コーヒーがほしいのですが……
blocks.en: I would like some coffee, but... (if it's no trouble)

blocks.text: The usual **target** particle, plus an old, written use meaning "and" in lists: 靴に指輪に帽子. The set phrase **それに** means "besides, in addition".

blocks.jp: 雨が降っている。それに、風も強い。
blocks.en: It is raining. On top of that, the wind is strong.

items: **Noun + で**: place or means; **predicate + で**: て-form of だ.
**Noun + が**: subject; **complete clause + が**: but.
**に**: target; in lists, "and"; **それに**: besides.
Check what comes before the kana and how the phrase ends.

questions.instruction: What is で in お元気で?
questions.note: A set phrase using the connective form of だ.

questions.instruction: What is で in 図書館で勉強する?
questions.note: A noun followed by で marks where it happens.

questions.instruction: What does で do in さくらはきれいで優しい?
questions.note: The て-form of だ connects predicates.

questions.prompt: お店に行ったが、パンがなかった。
questions.note: A connector after a complete clause.

questions.instruction: How do you tell the subject が from the connector が?
options: The subject が follows a noun; the connector follows a full clause
The connector が follows a noun
The subject が ends a sentence

questions.instruction: What does a sentence-final が do?
questions.prompt: コーヒーがほしいのですが……
questions.note: The listener fills in the rest.

questions.instruction: What does に mean in 靴に指輪に帽子?
questions.note: An old written use of に.
それ + に: on top of that.

questions.prompt: The connector が can come right after a plain noun.
questions.note: A connector needs a complete clause before it.
The て-form of だ links descriptions.
